_note: The scientific missions of MARS! / Red Dust City, one a day, as the sheets in the missions/ folder give them (MARS_Mission_NN_….pdf, one page each) — written by tools/missions-json.py, which reads every sheet in the folder; run it again when a sheet changes. `days` says which mission the crew are on each day of the run (day → mission number): as shipped the sheets follow the days in sequence — 00 on day 1, 15 October, to 12 on day 13, 27 October — and the Science officer changes a day's mission from the desk's Science tab, which writes this map. `missions` carries each sheet's words: its number and title (the file's — the number printed on the sheet is kept as sheetNo where it is another), the central question, the Morning, Afternoon and EVA parts as lines (a line in capitals is a heading, one starting with • a bullet, one starting with → a pointer), the question for the community hour in English and German as the sheet has them, the material it needs, and the sheet's file. A sheet that is a copy of another's PDF (standing in until it is written) keeps its title and carries no words — `placeholder` names the file it copies. The Today's Mission panel at the head of the mission dashboard shows the day's mission from here and links to its sheet at /missions/<file>.

missions.title: Energy Budget
missions.question: How much of our lives runs on electricity, and what is indispensable for us?
morning: • Read the power sockets / meters (record the values).
• Categorize devices by function: eating / living / research / body / communication.
• Calculate how many Wh an activity costs:
→ a pot of coffee, one day of hydroponics, 1× feeding the grasshoppers, 1× eating.
• What does a Habitat need in order to live?
afternoon: THE VALUE OF A KILOWATT-HOUR – decision experiment
Scenario: We have 1 kWh per day. What can we continue doing, what should we stop?
Create an individual plan and then make a joint decision.
HUMAN POWER – how much work is in a coffee?
• time how long until the water boils
→ How much human work is in everyday things?
→ Which of our Earth habits would we want to pay for with energy?
eva: • where energy is used in public space / everyday life
Ask: What would happen if tomorrow no electricity were available? What could be replaced with human labor, and what could not?

community.en: What do you use electricity for that you would not want to give up?
community.de: Welchen Prozess / welche Maschine, die auf Strom läuft, würdest du auf gar keinen Fall aufgeben wollen?

missions.materials: Pen/Paper, laptop, electricity meters, power bike, pedometer (?)

missions.title: Trust the System
missions.question: Do you trust machines over your own senses?
morning: SITUATION SCENARIOS – check measured values / presentation:
“Die Luft ist schlecht” (“The air is bad”).
“Der CO₂-Wert ist gestiegen” (“The CO₂ level has risen”).
• Where do I get that from?
afternoon: TWO INFORMATION SOURCES: own perception vs. sensors
Science Officer deliberately seeks discrepancies between measurement and perception, describes and reflects which information source they trust more and why.
Example: The air feels really stale, although O2 and CO2 sensors say everything is in order
→ technical systems / objects: more objective, precise, competent?
eva: • Why do we obey / follow the sign?
• What happens if we ignore it?
• Who decides what this sign means?

community.en: Would you trust a machine when it tells you that everything is in order?
community.de: Würdest du einer Maschine vertrauen wenn sie dir sagt dass alles in Ordnung ist?

missions.materials: Paper / pen or laptop; voice recorder; photo paper; photo printer; sensors (Habitat).

missions.title: Care as a Finite Resource
missions.question: The world needs care. But what if care was a finite resource – how would we distribute who and what gets cared for, what gets neglected?
morning: • Robot dog refuses to enter the EVA
afternoon: Throughout the day, document acts of care:
Log the time and what happened.
eva: Who cares for a place that belongs to all of us / belongs to none of us?
• Document disrepair, waste, graffiti, things that are broken or missing
• Humans that need care (e.g. difficult terrain, a person sitting alone)

community.en: What did you care for today?
community.de: Um was hast du dich heute gekümmert?

missions.materials: Stopwatch; paper & pen or laptop; possibly a voice recorder; photo paper; printed pictures

missions.title: How Humans Collaborate
missions.question: How do we still work together, if we are on different planets or if we see the world differently?
morning: Build something in 20 minutes. One person sees a picture and explains it; the others build.
• send a message every two minutes
• time until the thing is built properly
• how many errors occur during the day
• how many acts of communication are needed
afternoon: Building a whole from the pieces:

Fictitious scenario: large water-recycling station arrives tomorrow. All astronauts get a separate letter of instructions that doesn’t have the whole picture, but only parts. They need to come to a common solution through verbal communication.
eva: • Find 5 specific things and document them (astronaut inside the habitat has the list of things).
• Communication is only possible every 5 minutes.

community.en: What information would you send to astronauts who cannot see the outside? What is one thing happening back home / in Karlsruhe that we should know about?
community.de: Was ist eine Sache die zu Hause / in Karlsruhe grade passiert, über die wir auf dem Mars Bescheid wissen sollten? Was sollten Astronauten, die die Erde grade nicht sehen können, über sie wissen?

missions.materials: Building blocks with laminated photos of results; stopwatches; paper & pen or laptop, photo camera

missions.title: Waterways
missions.question: Humans cannot survive without water. How do we take care and notice water?
morning: Map where water enters and leaves the Habitat:
Where is water used in the Habitat? Where is water lost? Where does it flow? Where does it stand still?
Track water consumption by plants, crickets and human consumption.
Ask ground control for average rainfall on Marktplatz a day/a year
afternoon: Draw a visual map of the journey of a single drop of water as it travels through the habitat, informed by the learning of the morning – make more than one drawing for more than one journey
eva: • places where water can be collected or is lost
Ask: “How would our water consumption change if we could only use the water of our immediate surroundings?”

community.en: How are you saving water? What is your favorite spot with water in the city?
community.de: Wie sparst du Wasser in deinem täglichen Leben? Was ist dein Lieblingsort mit Wasser in der oder um die Stadt herum?

missions.materials: Camera; maybe photo printer; paper for mapping or laptop.

missions.title: School of McGyver
missions.question: If we can’t buy what we need, can we invent, make, repair or reuse?
morning: Make something that improves life in the Habitat.
afternoon: “Make something that tells the story of life for someone who has never been here.”
eva: Fictitious scenario: THE MARKETPLACE AS RESOURCE
“Name 5 objects from the marketplace that could be used as a resource. Which ones and why?”
• size, weight, value (e.g. place – waste? in Habitat?)
Make something that tells the story of life for someone who has never been here.

community.en: Which object from Earth would you take with you because you cannot live without it? If you could only take 1 thing, what would it be?

missions.materials: Craft materials (scissors, glue, gaffa tape; toolbox); photo paper; photo printer; voice recorder.

missions.title: Mars Myths
missions.question: What are the stories we tell each other to create sense out of chaos?
morning: Investigate historical / religious rule systems (with help of ground control) and extract different kinds of rules:
• What happens when a rule is broken?
afternoon: • What function does religion have in a society?
• What rituals are central to religious meaning-making?
• Which rituals, actions and objects are central for the survival of the community in the Habitat, and what could they become in a Mars religion?
• Invent rituals and myths (mythological justification for things & actions).
How could we ritualize everyday actions and mythologize them into an order in the Habitat?
Example: garbage receives a small ceremony / becomes a symbol as the guardian of waste; think about a translation from outside to inside making a small ritual action when you come inside from EVA
eva: Observe the marketplace and identify actions that may be important for the survival of the community:
• bakery / market: exchange, including human exchange

community.en: What rituals do you follow in your everyday life?
community.de: Welche Rituale hast du in deinem täglichen Leben?

missions.materials: paper / pen or laptop; photo paper; possibly craft materials, voice recorder

missions.title: Know Thy Neighbors
missions.question: We don’t live on this world alone. What do we actually know about the more-than-human (and human) neighbors?
morning: Short questionnaire about the crickets without looking at them first:
• Do they show responsibility towards each other?
• Do we feel responsible for them?
20-minute pure watching: no feeding, no touching, no interaction. Note concrete actions, behaviors and interactions, differences and reactions to each other.
Do the questionnaire again – did anything change?
afternoon: Choose one thing in the Habitat — a plant, cricket, sensor, piece of furniture, water tank, robot, etc.
Describe the Habitat for 20 minutes entirely from that entity’s perspective:
• What might it “know” about the astronauts?
• What would be important to it that humans overlook?
Then compare the different perspectives: What becomes visible when we stop taking the human perspective as the default?
eva: Observe and document people on the MARS!platz:
• How do the people who pass through the marketplace differ from the people who work there / live nearby?
• Which relationships between people can we identify?
• Which forms of use of the place are there?
• Optional interview: brief information about their perspective?

community.en: When does a stranger become a neighbor? What makes a good neighborhood?
community.de: Wann wird aus einem Fremden ein Nachbar? Was macht gute Nachbarschaft aus?

missions.materials: Pen/Paper or laptop, voice recorder, the crickets, photo camera, maybe photo printer

missions.title: Space and Spaces
missions.question: Placemaking is an intentional activity – how do we use the spaces we are given, how do we create a space that feels a certain way?
morning: Map the Habitat by scenes / activities: sleeping, working, eating, retreat, storage, community, paths.
→ Make a scene map of the Habitat.
→ Observation period: Who is where, when and why?
→ Planned spatial layout vs. actually used space.
afternoon: At the marketplace: where do people stand, where do they stay, where do encounters happen, where do people avoid each other?
eva: Use chalk to delineate parts of the habitat from the prototypes we haven’t built on marktplatz and mark them as one of two zones: encounter or avoidance
Reflection: How much private space does a person need? How much public space does a society need?

community.en: Where in public space do you feel at home, and what gives you a feeling of “belonging”?
community.de: Wo im öffentlichen Raum fühlst du dich zu Hause, wo gehörst du hin?

missions.title: Art and Beauty
missions.question: Does MARS! need beauty? What makes life a good life?
morning: • What is needed for a good life?
afternoon: BEAUTY & THE VISIBLE IN THE HABITAT
What can make the Habitat more beautiful?
• Is the place more pleasant now?
• Do I want to stay longer?
• Does the place feel more “at home”?
eva: • What makes people want to live here?
→ Find a spot that is “beautiful” and describe what makes it beautiful to you and why.
Consider the contrasting properties of the place and the feeling of beauty.

community.en: What would you not throw out of your apartment, even if it is actually not necessary for survival?
community.de: Welchen Gegenstand würdest du nie aus deiner Wohnung entfernen, selbst wenn er nicht für dein unmittelbares Überleben wichtig ist?

missions.materials: Pen/paper, laptop, materials around the habitat (craft material, toolbox), voice recorder, camera

missions.title: The Power of Words
morning: Create a dictionary for life on Mars (how we talk about change).
What does, for example, the following mean?
afternoon: THE OTHER POINT OF VIEW – creative writing exercise for empathy.
Choose 1 event that happened in the Habitat during the day (doesn’t necessarily have happened to the describing officer). Describe it from:
• the perspective of the astronaut experiencing it
• the perspective of an object involved
• the perspective of a person on Earth who only heard about it
eva: Rename places and objects on the marketplace:
• Who gets to name places and objects?
• Is naming a form of ownership?

community.en: Are we allowed to simply rename the MARS!platz?

missions.materials: Pen/Paper, laptop, voice recorder, cardboard and marker to rename things on marktplatz?
